card.name: Last word before a dash or aside
card.fires_on: The final word of a short complete clause in casual web text, right where a dash, comma or ellipsis could come next. Often a bullet point or reassurance such as 'don't worry' or 'is key'.

modes.label: End of bullet statement
modes.description: Last word of a short advice or tip clause in a list, before a dash or the next sentence.
modes.example: - White space is<< okay>>. - Integrate images and rich media

modes.label: Reassurance 'worry'
modes.description: The word worry after don't, followed by a continuation.
modes.example: but don't<< worry>>, they weren't modern tourists

modes.label: Clause-final noun or verb
modes.description: A closing noun or verb of a plain clause, where the sentence could trail off or continue after a dash.
modes.example: Yawning is something many animals<< do>>, from lizards and snakes

card.writes: It promotes ellipsis marks and suppresses dash-and-paragraph-break endings, so it nudges toward trailing punctuation instead.
card.plain: It fires on the last word of a short casual sentence, just before the writer might add a dash or trail off.
